exposure: Cervical length (CL) measured by transabdominal ultrasound at 20-24+6 weeks of gestation
cohort: 202 singleton pregnant women (101 with spontaneous preterm birth and 101 with full-term delivery) matched for maternal age, BMI, preterm birth history, cesarean section history, and pregnancy interval >=5 years
finding: Transabdominal ultrasound measurement of cervical length at 20-24+6 weeks of gestation is a potential screening tool for spontaneous preterm birth, particularly for births before 32 and 28 weeks, with shorter cervical lengths associated with higher risk.
